quote: it says solar, no cost, and you get a, Tesla Powerwall, and stuff like that.
stewart_read: Customer's actual draw to the call is the Powerwall/no-cost framing from the ad — a concrete cross-sell/interest anchor the rep never reflects back or reinforces later.
coaching_implication: Rep should have flagged this specifically for the closer brief and tied the appointment back to it ("we'll make sure the specialist covers the Powerwall option Tuesday") rather than letting it pass as a generic note.

quote: But I'm not interested in the PPA at all.
stewart_read: Customer states a firm financing preference shaped by prior competitor conversations; rep logs it but never asks which companies or what he was shown to sharpen the closer's approach.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have deliberately avoided digging deeper to stay in scope and not get pulled into a financing debate.
coaching_implication: A single question — "what did those other companies show you on the purchase side?" — would have armed the closer without violating scope.

quote: There is not a pocket cost or any of these no matter what you look at with us. So just wanted to make that clear.
stewart_read: Rep makes a definitive claim about all product/financing paths having no out-of-pocket cost — this is closer-tier financial content stated as certain fact.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep intended this only to reassure on a narrow point (down payment), not to answer the PPA-vs-purchase question, so it may be a limited reassurance rather than full scope creep.
coaching_implication: Should redirect general cost claims to the specialist entirely: "the specialist will walk through exact costs for each option Tuesday."

quote: I will I will prefer if they call me before they show up, like, to go over the details just like we're going right now.
stewart_read: This is a timing/channel objection to the in-person visit; rep explains the policy reason but doesn't offer any bridge beyond restating the in-person requirement.
alternative_hypothesis: Company likely has a hard no-phone-consult policy, so the rep may have had no room to concede — reactive language, but constrained by real policy.
coaching_implication: Even within policy, rep could reframe: "Totally fair — that's actually why we send the specialist in person, so you get everything covered live like we're doing now, just with the full design in hand."

quote: But if they can call me and we can talk about it before they come to the house. Because my wife and I, we have eight automated schedules,
stewart_read: Customer flags a co-owner (wife) scheduling conflict directly tied to why he wants a phone pre-screen; rep never circles back to confirm whether the wife will actually be present Tuesday.
coaching_implication: Rep should have asked directly, "will your wife be able to join at 5 on Tuesday?" to lock co-owner attendance per protocol.

quote: all we ask of the homeowner is you just have a credit score of at least 670. Is that gonna be an issue for you guys at all?
stewart_read: Rep runs the credit qualifier verbatim to schema threshold and gets a clean pass — solid procedural execution amid an otherwise improvised call.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed here; this is the correct baseline execution.

quote: but the delivery fees are the ones that are, you know, a little bit upsetting.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep the actual pain point (delivery fees, not usage) and even builds his own analogy for it — the rep never reflects this back or uses it to flip against the utility.
coaching_implication: This was the moment to flip: "that's exactly the fee structure solar doesn't touch — what you're really paying for is the delivery, not the power," per coaching_philosophy.objection_inversion.
